rendered_html: 📔 Regulatory Bulletin — 11 September 2026 (Weekly) Executive Summary • HKMA has published a current circular on private market investments for registered institutions, classified under securities/investment products; the registered evidence does not expose its operative text or a deadline. • HKMA’s Phase 2B Hong Kong Taxonomy consultation is open to all authorised institutions until 7 October 2026; management may wish to decide whether to respond and identify potentially affected sustainable-finance claims and data. • Singapore’s legislative-stage scam-countermeasures development is a useful benchmark for account-restriction and customer-access trade-offs, but does not establish a Hong Kong requirement. Hong Kong 🟡 Circular on Private Market Investments 🇭🇰 Item ID: item-20260909-hkma-circulars-ebe8a08cb8 ⏰ Deadline: No source deadline stated Products: Investment products HKMA has published a current circular, “Circular on Private Market Investments”, issued on 9 September 2026 for Registered Institutions. The repository classifies it under Wealth Management & MPF — Securities/investment products. The registered evidence does not expose the circular’s operative text, scope, deadline, transition, exemption or explicit expectation, so it does not establish an obligation or supervisory expectation. Relevant institutions may obtain the official circular text and document its scope, authority and dates before deciding whether any change work is needed. Source: Circular on Private Market Investments 🟡 Consultation on Phase 2B prototype of Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance 🇭🇰 Item ID: item-20260907-hkma-consultations-4ec8d8ecfe ⏰ Deadline: 7 October 2026 Products: Sustainable lending, investment products HKMA has opened a consultation for all authorised institutions on a Phase 2B prototype of the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance. Comments close on 7 October 2026, and the repository records the consultation as open. This is a consultation rather than a binding taxonomy or new compliance requirement; sustainable lending and investment products or related claims may have product-governance, data and disclosure dependencies if the prototype is finalised. Source: Consultation on Phase 2B prototype of Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance SG/UK/GLOBAL Benchmark Comparable overseas developments and commercial/control benchmarks. They do not establish Hong Kong requirements. 🟡 Second Reading of the Scams (Countermeasures) and Other Matters Bill — Wrap-Up Speech 🇸🇬 Item ID: item-20260909-daily-exploratory-search-9fdc3e64ee ⏰ Deadline: October 2026 (exact date not stated) Products: Deposit accounts, payments Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs described proposed Account Disabling, Disclosure and Service Limitation Orders in a Second Reading wrap-up speech, including information exchange with service providers and obligations imposed by those orders. It said local banks will offer an LPBA or alternative basic account from October 2026 to affected Singapore citizens or permanent residents except in limited cases, without stating an exact date. This is a legislative-stage government speech, not an enacted rule or MAS instrument, and may inform monitoring of the operational and customer-access trade-off in scam-related account restrictions without creating a Hong Kong obligation. Source: Second Reading of the Scams (Countermeasures) and Other Matters Bill — Wrap-Up Speech Watch List • Monitor the final Singapore Bill provisions, commencement date and exclusions; the available source does not establish them. • Monitor the outcome of HKMA’s Phase 2B taxonomy consultation, including any final scope, criteria and implementation timing. Weekly Trend This week’s validated developments include a current HKMA circular on private market investments, a sustainable-finance taxonomy consultation and a scam-intervention design benchmark. The circular’s operative content is not available in the registered evidence; the consultation is open, while the Singapore item remains a comparable legislative-stage benchmark rather than a Hong Kong requirement.
